claims.text: Rebalancing moves rows between shards when a shard is added or one has grown too large, and every row must stay findable while it moves.

For consecutive ids, (id % 4, id % 5) repeats every 20 ids and matches only for id mod 20 in 0-3; of the 16 movers in each 20, 4 (id % 5 = 4) go to new shard 4 and 12 to another old shard: 80% move, 60% between old shards.
With a shard map, the bucket is key % 64 and a table row per bucket names the shard; adding a shard reassigns some rows of the map, and only orders in reassigned buckets change shard.
77 % 64 = 13 and 13 % 4 = 1, so with the initial map (bucket % 4) order 77 is in bucket 13 on shard 1, which is not among buckets 0-11 moved to shard 4.
Every read and write looks up the shard map before choosing a connection, so the map is a dependency of every request; if no copy of it can be read, no request can be routed.
claims.source_hint: Follows from the design (outline item 5); condition: the map is the only source of bucket-to-shard placement

claims.text: While a bucket moves, its writes go only to the old shard until the map row changes, every write the old shard took after the copy must also reach the new shard before the switch, then writes go only to the new shard; writes on both shards give two versions.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5 and misconception 2; general reasoning about copy-then-switch

claims.text: The bucket count is fixed when the map is created: every key's bucket is computed from it, so changing 64 moves many keys to another bucket, as changing % 4 to % 5 does. Each bucket lives whole on one shard, so 64 buckets fill at most 64 shards.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 6; rebalance.sql shard_map has bucket as primary key (one shard per bucket)

claims.text: Đơn Hàng is not sharded at stage-3; rebalance.sql only counts (comment lines 1-4: 'Nothing is moved: each query only counts') and uses the order id as the key.
In PostgreSQL, count(*) FILTER (WHERE cond) counts only rows satisfying cond; % on integers returns the remainder; round(numeric, 1) rounds to one decimal.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 4.2.7 Aggregate Expressions (FILTER); 9.3 Mathematical Functions and Operators

claims.text: CREATE TEMP TABLE creates a temporary table; generate_series(0, 63) yields 64 rows 0-63; the INSERT assigns bucket b to shard b % 4, 16 buckets per shard; UPDATE ... WHERE bucket < 12 moves buckets 0-11, three from each old shard.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: SQL CREATE TABLE (TEMPORARY); 9.25 Set Returning Functions; rebalance.sql lines 15-26; output 'INSERT 0 64', 'UPDATE 12'
